documents.title: Diabetes / HTN follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Subjective
55M with T2DM, HTN, HLD, obesity. Fasting. Got home Sunday from a two-week run. Feels fine. Says he takes everything; pill organizer refilled every Sunday. Diet "is the hard part," lots of drive-thru. No exercise to speak of. Home BP log: mostly 142-150 over 88-94.
Denies chest pain, dyspnea, palpitations, numbness in feet.

Medications
metformin 1000 mg twice daily
lisinopril 20 mg daily
amlodipine 5 mg daily
hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily
atorvastatin 40 mg daily

Objective
BP 142/93  HR 81  RR 15  T 36.6  SpO2 97%  Wt 101.6 kg  BMI 31.9
Appears well. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. No peripheral edema. Feet intact, pulses good.

Assessment / Plan
T2DM - A1c and fasting glucose today.
HTN - still 140s over low 90s here and at home on three drugs. Sees cardiology on 01/27 and wants them to handle any change; copy of our readings and today's labs to go to them.
HLD - lipid panel today.
Obesity - weight unchanged. Encouraged a 20-minute walk on his 34-hour restarts.
F/u July.

documents.title: Labs 01/14
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Fasting glucose 138, A1c 7.2. TC 190, HDL 35, LDL 120, TG 250.
Triglycerides up from 150 in July; HDL down to 35. Likely diet. Sent to patient with diet tips (sugary drinks, fried food, late meals). Faxed to cardiology for 01/27 visit.

documents.title: Cardiology follow-up letter
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
CARDIOLOGY — FOLLOW-UP VISIT
Date of service: 01/27/2020
Re: Lamar Bryant, DOB 02/26/1964
To: primary care physician

Mr. Bryant is a 55-year-old truck driver with longstanding type 2 diabetes, hypertension and hyperlipidemia who comes back to us for his routine blood pressure follow-up. His endocrinology review last summer was unremarkable. He tells us he is taking his medicines as prescribed. He finds the recommended diet hard to keep to and is not exercising, which he puts down to his work hours.

Current medications as listed today: lisinopril 20 mg daily, amlodipine 5 mg daily, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily; he also takes metformin and atorvastatin.
Allergies: NKDA.
Family history: father with type 2 diabetes, hypertension and obstructive sleep apnea; mother with hypertension and hyperlipidemia; a paternal uncle with coronary artery disease.

Examination: BP 146/92 mmHg. His pressure has been above goal at each of his last three visits. BMI 32 kg/m2. The examination is otherwise unremarkable apart from obesity.

Laboratory (primary care, 01/14/2020): fasting glucose 138 mg/dL, HbA1c 7.2%, total cholesterol 190, HDL 35, LDL 120, triglycerides 250 mg/dL.

Assessment:
1. Essential hypertension, above goal on three agents.
2. Metabolic syndrome: central obesity, low HDL, elevated triglycerides, hypertension and type 2 diabetes.
3. Hyperlipidemia on atorvastatin.

Plan: No change to his medications today. We reviewed salt restriction, meal choices on the road and building in some walking. Continue home blood pressure readings. Follow-up in six months.

documents.title: Refills / mail order
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi. With all this virus stuff my company says we should use the mail order pharmacy so we aren't going into stores. Can you send all 5 of my meds there for 90 days? Still driving, we're essential. Card info is the same.

documents.title: RE: Refills / mail order
documents.author: RN
documents.body:
Hi Lamar, all five prescriptions were sent to your plan's mail-order pharmacy this morning, 90-day supply with refills. Allow about 10 days for delivery; we sent a 30-day bridge to your local pharmacy in case the box is late.
If you get fever, cough or shortness of breath on the road, text or call us. Masks and hand sanitizer at the truck stops, please.

documents.title: Diabetes and Hypertension Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
In person, masked. Fasting.
Working steadily through the pandemic, more miles than ever. Diet worse: "everything is drive-thru now." Takes all his pills. Home log from the cab: 145-156 / 88-96 most mornings. No chest pain, palpitations or shortness of breath. No headaches.

Meds: metformin 1000 BID, lisinopril 20 daily, amlodipine 5 daily, HCTZ 25 daily, atorvastatin 40 daily. NKDA.

Exam: BP 148/92, HR 68, RR 15, T 36.5, SpO2 96%. Weight 102.7 kg, BMI 32.2.
Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. No edema. Feet normal.

Plan:
1. T2DM - A1c, fasting glucose today. Metformin unchanged.
2. HTN - high at home and here. Cardiology appointment 07/30; will send today's numbers and his log there.
3. HLD - lipid panel today.
4. Diet discussed at length; he agreed to swap soda for water/seltzer and to try to keep one cooler meal a day.
Next: physical in October.

Fasting glucose 158, A1c 7.4. TC 210, HDL 35, LDL 145, TG 300.
A1c and lipids both drifted up with the diet changes he described. Portal message to patient: continue meds, the soda swap and cooler meals; recheck at physical / winter. Faxed to cardiology for 07/30.

documents.body:
CARDIOLOGY CLINIC NOTE
Visit: 07/30/2020
Patient: Lamar Bryant (DOB 02/26/1964)
cc: primary care

Interval history: Mr. Bryant, 56, with type 2 diabetes and hypertension, is back for follow-up of his blood pressure. He says he has not missed doses of his antihypertensives, but the readings he takes at home have stayed over target. He brought a log, mostly mid-140s to mid-150s systolic. No chest pain, no palpitations, no shortness of breath.

Medications: lisinopril 20 mg daily, amlodipine 5 mg daily, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg daily, metformin.
Allergies: NKDA.
Social: former smoker, 20 pack-years. Alcohol rarely. Long-haul driver.

Vitals: BP 152/94, HR 78, BMI 32.

Labs from primary care 07/21/2020: fasting plasma glucose 158, HbA1c 7.4%, total cholesterol 210, HDL 35, LDL 145, triglycerides 300.

Impression: Hypertension, home and office readings above goal on lisinopril, amlodipine and hydrochlorothiazide.

Plan: Continue the present regimen without change. Keep the home log and bring it to each visit. Return in one year, sooner if needed.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
ANNUAL EXAM - 56 y/o M

Interval: Cardiology 07/30 - no change in BP meds, follow up in a year. Still driving full-time. Kept up the seltzer swap most weeks. No new complaints.

Problems: T2DM since 2004; essential HTN; hyperlipidemia; obesity.
Medications: metformin 1000 mg BID; lisinopril 20 mg daily; amlodipine 5 mg daily; HCTZ 25 mg qAM; atorvastatin 40 mg daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
Social: married. Former smoker (quit 03/2011, 20 pack-years). Alcohol 1-2/month.

ROS: negative in detail.

Vitals: BP 146/87, HR 75, RR 18, T 36.4, SpO2 96%. Wt 101.1 kg, Ht 177.4 cm, BMI 32.1.
Exam:
Gen - well, masked.
HEENT - normal. Neck - supple, no nodes.
Heart - RRR, no murmur. Lungs - clear.
Abd - obese, soft, nontender.
Skin - normal. Ext - no edema.
Foot exam - intact skin, 2+ pulses, normal monofilament both feet.
Neuro - nonfocal.
PHQ-2 0.

A/P
1. Preventive: flu shot today. Hep B and Shingrix series complete. Tdap 2015. Colonoscopy due 2024. PSA normal 2019; repeat next year per his preference.
2. T2DM: A1c 7.4 in July. BMP and urine albumin/creatinine today. Recheck A1c in January.
3. HTN: 146/87. Continue regimen as set by cardiology.
4. HLD: continue atorvastatin 40.
5. Obesity: stable.
CBC today. Video visit in January if he is on the road.

documents.title: Physical labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
BMP: creatinine 0.99, eGFR 89, K 4.0 normal. Glucose 139, high, fasting; in keeping with his diabetes, A1c at the January visit. Urine albumin/creatinine 10, normal. CBC normal.
No action beyond the diabetes follow-up already planned. Released with note.

documents.title: Video Visit - Diabetes / BP
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video visit; patient in his truck, parked at a rest area in Indiana. Identity confirmed. Consent for video visit obtained.

He got labs done at our draw station Saturday 01/16 before heading out: A1c 7.3, fasting glucose 141.

Says he has been more careful since the summer: fewer sodas, packs a cooler. Home BP lately 130-138 over 82-88 (read several off his phone). Taking all medications. No chest pain, no breathlessness, no foot problems.

Meds unchanged: metformin 1000 mg BID, lisinopril 20 mg, amlodipine 5 mg, HCTZ 25 mg, atorvastatin 40 mg.

Exam limited to video: well appearing, speaking full sentences, no distress.

Assessment/Plan
- T2DM: A1c 7.3, down from 7.4. Keep going with the diet changes. Metformin unchanged.
- HTN: home readings better, 130s/80s. Continue.
- HLD: atorvastatin 40; lipids in July.
- COVID-19 vaccine: he is interested; told him to sign up through the state site or a pharmacy as soon as his group opens.
Office visit in July, fasting.

documents.title: Follow-up: diabetes, hypertension, lipids
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: 57-year-old, fasting. Feels well. Both COVID vaccines done in the spring. Still packing the cooler most runs, but admits the past month slipped. Home BP mostly 128-138 / 80-86. Taking medicines daily. No chest pain, no dyspnea, no claudication, no foot issues. Has a cardiology visit later this month; he wants to ask them about "a new heart pill" he read about.

Meds: metformin 1000 mg BID, lisinopril 20 mg qd, amlodipine 5 mg qd, HCTZ 25 mg qd, atorvastatin 40 mg qd.

O: BP 132/85, HR 66, RR 16, T 36.6, SpO2 97%. Wt 100.0 kg, BMI 31.8.
NAD. Heart RRR. Lungs clear. Ext no edema. Feet: normal skin and pulses, monofilament intact.

A/P:
1. T2DM: A1c, fasting glucose today. Continue metformin and diet work.
2. HTN: 132/85 here, home in the 130s. Better. Continue all three.
3. HLD: lipid panel today. He will take his cardiology question to them on the 27th; we'll send today's results.
4. Lung cancer screening: new USPSTF criteria (age 50-80, 20 pack-years, quit within 15 years) now include him - 20 pack-years, quit 03/2011. Shared decision-making done: reviewed benefit, false positives, follow-up imaging, radiation dose, and that screening stops once 15 years have passed since quitting (03/2026). He wants to do it. Low-dose CT ordered; he'll schedule for September when he has a home stretch.
5. Eye exam due next month; he has an optometry appointment.
RTC October physical.

documents.title: Cardiology visit letter
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
CARDIOLOGY OUTPATIENT VISIT
Date: 07/27/2021
Patient: Lamar Bryant, 57
Referring/primary: primary care physician

Purpose of visit: review of his overall cardiovascular risk and discussion of adding a second lipid-lowering agent to his atorvastatin.

History: Mr. Bryant has type 2 diabetes, hypertension and hyperlipidemia. We last saw him a year ago for blood pressure running high at home. Since then he reports no new symptoms and feels well. He continues to take his medications every day. He came in asking about a new medicine to lower his risk of heart disease further; he had read about a recent trial in which people on a new drug had fewer heart attacks.

Medications reviewed: atorvastatin 40 mg daily, amlodipine 5 mg daily, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily, lisinopril, metformin.
Allergies: NKDA.
Family history: father with diabetes, hypertension and sleep apnea; mother with hypertension and hyperlipidemia; paternal uncle with coronary artery disease.
Social history: long-haul truck driver; former smoker, 20 pack-years; alcohol 1-2 drinks per month.

Examination: BP 132/84. General, cardiac, pulmonary and vascular examination unremarkable.

Laboratory (primary care, 07/13/2021): HbA1c 7.2%, fasting glucose 158 mg/dL, total cholesterol 220, HDL 35, LDL 145, triglycerides 200 mg/dL.

Assessment: Type 2 diabetes, hypertension and hyperlipidemia; blood pressure at goal today.

Plan: We talked through the option of adding lipid-lowering therapy on top of his statin. He will continue his current medications as they are.

OPTOMETRY — DIABETIC EYE EXAM REPORT
Date of exam: 08/10/2021
Patient: Lamar Bryant

Best corrected acuity: OD 20/20, OS 20/20-.
Pupils equal and reactive, no afferent defect. IOP normal OU.
Dilated fundus exam OU: discs pink and sharp, C/D 0.3. Maculae flat and dry. No dot-blot hemorrhages, microaneurysms, cotton wool spots, exudates or new vessels. Periphery attached and clear.

reports.study: Low-dose CT chest for lung cancer screening
reports.text:
LOW-DOSE CT CHEST, LUNG CANCER SCREENING (baseline)
Indication: Former smoker, 20 pack-years, quit 2011. Asymptomatic.
Technique: Low-dose helical CT of the chest without IV contrast.
Comparison: None.
Findings:
Lungs: No pulmonary nodules. No consolidation, effusion or pneumothorax. Airways patent.
Mediastinum: No lymphadenopathy. Heart size normal. No pericardial effusion. Thoracic aorta normal in caliber.
Upper abdomen: Unremarkable on limited images.
Bones: No suspicious lesion.
reports.conclusion: Lung-RADS 1: negative. Continue annual screening with low-dose CT in 12 months.

documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
ANNUAL PREVENTIVE VISIT

57-year-old man. Interval: cardiology 07/27 discussed adding a second cholesterol medicine; he is continuing his current regimen. Eye exam 08/2021 without retinopathy. Lung screening CT 09/14 negative (Lung-RADS 1). Feels well.

PMH: T2DM (2004), HTN, HLD, obesity.
Meds: metformin 1000 mg BID, lisinopril 20 mg daily, amlodipine 5 mg daily, HCTZ 25 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
FH: father T2DM/HTN/OSA; mother HTN/HLD; paternal uncle CAD.
SH: married; trucker; ex-smoker since 03/2011, 20 pk-yr; alcohol 1-2/month.

ROS: negative.

Vitals: BP 133/85, HR 69, RR 17, T 36.7, SpO2 98%. Wt 100.4 kg, Ht 178.0 cm, BMI 31.7.
General: well. HEENT: normal. Neck: no thyromegaly or nodes.
Cardiac: regular, no murmur. Lungs: clear.
Abdomen: soft, nontender.
Skin: no lesions of concern. Extremities: no edema.
Feet: no ulceration, pulses 2+, monofilament sensation normal.
PHQ-2: 0.

Plan
1. Immunizations: flu today. Pneumococcal vaccine indicated with diabetes - PCV20 today (single dose). COVID booster: eligible; he will get it at a pharmacy.
2. PSA after discussion today (last 0.9 in 2019); he wants it.
3. T2DM: A1c 7.2 in July. BMP and urine albumin/creatinine today.
4. HTN: 133/85, at goal-ish. Continue.
5. HLD: continue atorvastatin 40.
6. Lung screening: annual LDCT, next 09/2022.
7. Colon: due 2024.
CBC today. Diabetes follow-up January.

documents.title: Physical labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Creatinine 1.0, eGFR 88, potassium 4.3. Glucose 141, high (fasting), consistent with his diabetes; A1c in January. Urine albumin/creatinine 11. CBC normal. PSA 1.0, stable.
Released to portal: kidney, urine, blood count and PSA normal; sugar high as expected, to go over at the diabetes visit.
